ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) and send the driver's account for review of the off-location "I'm Here" tap + flag_account

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that NS-1(ii) is met on the driver's own account rests solely on the driver's statement [F12], which the system records contradict: the tap was made 601 m from the pickup point [F5], the closest approach was 545 m [F1] and no arrival was ever recorded [F4]. System records override statements, so NS-1(ii) fails.

The 3 min 30 s stationary period [F2] satisfies NS-1(iii) only in duration, not in place: the entire wait was 600 m from the pickup point and the driver spent 0 s inside the radius after the tap [F5], so the wait was not 'at the pick-up point' as NS-1(iii) requires.

The 12:06 message 'I'm here already' [F8] is disproved by the GPS record [F1][F2][F5], so the mismatch was caused by the driver's position, not by any rider no-show; the rider's reply [F9] matches the system record and NS-1 requires a location the driver never reached.

Not contested and irrelevant to liability: charging exactly the published $6.61 with 1.0× surge [F6][F7] does not cure the failure of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii), which under NS-2 requires the full fee to be refunded.

Withdrawn in rebuttal and in any case ineffective: the driver's clean profile (873 d, 4.84, 502 trips, 0 upheld) [F17] cannot excuse the off-location arrival tap shown by the system record [F5][F1][F4], which NS-2 makes the basis for flag_account; profile facts never decide a case alone.

The rider's good standing [F16] is not the ground of the refund, and no driver-side finding beyond the arrival-button position was needed: NS-2 makes the refund mandatory once NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) are not cumulatively met [F1][F4][F5].
